members.name: order_flow_imbalance_v1
members.thesis: Cumulative order flow imbalance (OFI) — the running sum of signed trade volume classified as buyer-initiated or seller-initiated — predicts short-term price direction. When OFI diverges from price (e.g., OFI rising while price is flat), it signals latent buying pressure that will soon manifest in pr
entry_long: OFI_price_divergence == True AND OFI_momentum > 0 (flow says buy, price hasn't moved)
filters: skip first 5 min and last 10 min
1-min volume > 50th percentile of day's volume distribution
OFI direction aligns with NIFTY 50 intraday direction
weaknesses: Lee-Ready trade classification has ~15-20% misclassification rate, directly corrupting the OFI signal. In fast-moving markets, accuracy drops further.
Cumulative OFI is susceptible to large single-trade outliers (e.g., a block deal) that can flip the signal without genuine change in market sentiment.
The divergence signal (flow says X but price says Y) may simply reflect informed sellers distributing into buying flow, making the 'buy' signal a trap.

weaknesses: Tick direction is a noisy proxy for order flow — a single large sell order hitting the bid doesn't register as many downticks but represents significant selling pressure.
